events.text:
**Pick: Grand Haven, but expect a slow day anywhere.** I'd rate all four ports about 1 (below average) for pier salmon this week. The newest reports are from 2022-05-18, which is 6 days old.

| Port | Rating | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Grand Haven | 1 | A few coho from the pier, the only port with two methods reported |
| St. Joseph | 1 | An occasional coho, but pier reports there have been steady all spring |
| South Haven | 1 (low end) | Pier "remained slow" |
| Muskegon | 1 (low confidence) | No pier report at all |

**What the reports say**
- **Grand Haven:** "Pier anglers were catching a few coho salmon on alewives or while casting orange spoons" (Grand Haven, 2022-05-18). Earlier, pier fishing was slow, and orange spoons were working best (Grand Haven, 2022-04-27).
- **St. Joseph:** Pier anglers caught an occasional coho on spawn, and nightcrawlers caught catfish (St. Joseph, 2022-05-18). Earlier reports were similar: a few coho on spawn (St. Joseph, 2022-05-04 and 2022-04-27).
- **South Haven:** "Pier fishing remained slow but there was an occasional coho caught on spawn" (South Haven, 2022-05-18). Earlier reports were also poor: a few coho and steelhead on spawn (South Haven, 2022-05-04) and "very slow" (South Haven, 2022-04-20).
- **Muskegon:** The latest report covers boats only. They were "doing well catching salmon 35 to 90 feet down in 120 to 200 feet of water," on green and blue spoons and white flies (Muskegon, 2022-05-18). Grand Haven boats were also doing well, with salmon 30 to 120 feet down in 130 to 240 feet of water (Grand Haven, 2022-05-18).
- **Water temperature:** Buoy surface temperature, which is measured, averaged 52–53 F this past week. It fell 3–4 F over the week (St. Joseph and South Haven 53 F, -4 F; Grand Haven and Muskegon 52 F, -3 F).
- **Access:** None of the reports mention closed piers or launches.

**My read**
- The good catches are on boats well offshore, in deep water and often far down. I'd expect most salmon to be out there, not at the piers, so pier catches should stay at a few fish.
- A 3–4 F drop is modest. I wouldn't call it the sharp drop that signals an upwelling and brings salmon to the piers.
- Grand Haven gets the edge because it's the only pier with a recent report of fish taken two ways, on bait and on casting spoons. That is a thin edge.
- Muskegon's rating is a guess. The offshore bite there is good, but I have no pier information.
- If you go to St. Joseph or South Haven, fish spawn, since that's what has been catching coho there. At Grand Haven, try alewife or cast an orange spoon.

**Caveats**
- The database has no earlier seasons for this date, so I have no history to compare against.
- Current conditions gave only the weekly buoy summary. I had no wind forecast or modeled pierhead temperatures. Check the wind before you go, because onshore wind and rough water have made pier fishing difficult (St. Joseph, 2022-05-04).
